bash.description: GNU Bash; it forks, so it is built with Asyncify

modifications.what: the build: configures with the bundled readline and termcap and without bash's malloc, drops configure's -Wl,--fatal-warnings, and changes shell.c so main takes (argc, argv) as the C library calls it, with the environment from environ; Asyncify rewrites the program, told where its calls through a pointer reach fork
the build: configures make to start its jobs with posix_spawn and to wait for jobserver tokens without pselect; the make source is unmodified

the build; patches src/nano.c so TERM=xterm.js (or unset) falls back to xterm-256color and a SHELL that is not a path falls back to /bin/sh, and src/files.c and src/text.c so an executed command, the formatter and the linter are started with posix_spawn where nano forks, and the text a command filters is sent from a thread where a forked process sent it; builds ncurses with built-in terminfo entries
compile and link flags, and the counts (size_t and ssize_t) are printed with %zd where the source has %ld, which on WALI is wider

evtest.description: evtest, which lists the input devices and prints what one reports

modifications.what: compile and link flags, with the version named on the command line in place of the configure script's config.h; no source changes

vim.description: Vim, the modal text editor (the `normal` feature set)

modifications.file: core/utils/wasm/lib/ecmaos/termcap.c (in the repository; wasm/lib/ecmaos/termcap.c in the npm package @ecmaos/coreutils)
modifications.what: linked into the program: a termcap that finds no terminal, so Vim uses its builtin terminal entries

configure flags and defines (SYS_VIMRC_FILE, VIM_DEFAULTS_FILE, USE_SYSTEM, MODIFIED_BY, and <sys/wait.h> included), and one line of src/ui.c changed: inchar_loop's wait for a key stops at zero instead of waiting forever when the time already passed is taken off a wait of none
compile and link flags only; the source is unmodified. The archive is Debian's gzip copy of upstream's ed-1.22.5.tar.lz, since upstream publishes only lzip

lz4.description: lz4, and unlz4 and lz4cat (links to it)

modifications.what: compile and link flags only (with threads); the source is unmodified

doom.description: doom, id Software's Doom (doomgeneric) in a window on SDL 3; bring your own WAD, e.g. Freedoom (needs wlcomp running)

modifications.what: the build: compiles the doomgeneric engine without its other platform layers and its SDL_mixer sound and music modules
new file, linked into the program: the platform layer, which draws the engine's frames into a window on SDL 3 and turns SDL key events into Doom keys
new file, linked into the program: the engine's sound module, a mixer that plays the sound effect lumps through an SDL 3 audio stream

modifications.file: core/utils/wasm/lib/sdl.sh (in the repository; wasm/lib/sdl.sh and wasm/lib/sdl-gl/ in the npm package @ecmaos/coreutils)
modifications.what: builds SDL as a static library for a Unix program on Wayland: a software window surface for its Wayland driver, audio and joystick drivers of its own, and the other changes its header lists

modifications.file: core/utils/wasm/lib/wayland.sh (in the repository; wasm/lib/wayland.sh in the npm package @ecmaos/coreutils)
modifications.what: builds libwayland-client, -cursor and -egl as static libraries, with listener calls made without libffi

modifications.file: core/utils/wasm/lib/xkbcommon.sh (in the repository; wasm/lib/xkbcommon.sh in the npm package @ecmaos/coreutils)
modifications.what: builds libxkbcommon as a static library without meson; a missing Compose table is logged at debug level

screen.description: GNU screen, with ncurses: terminal multiplexer, and a serial console (screen /dev/ttyACM0 115200)

modifications.what: the build; patches screen.c so TERM=xterm.js (or unset) falls back to xterm-256color and a SHELL that is not a path falls back to /bin/sh; configured without PAM, utmp or the socket directory (sockets are in ~/.screen), and linked with Asyncify so it can fork; builds ncurses with built-in terminfo entries

aplay.description: aplay, ALSA's command line player: plays WAV and raw sound to the card behind /dev/snd/pcmC0D0p (aplay -l lists it; -D hw:0,0 is the card as it is, the default converts format, rate and channels), with alsa-lib

modifications.what: the build; alsa-lib is a static library without dlopen, the sequencer, rawmidi, hwdep, topology or use-case manager, reading /usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf; include/local.h loses its claim that the linker is GNU ld (WebAssembly's assembler has no .gnu.warning sections) and include/alsa-symbols.h makes the public names of versioned functions as weak aliases instead of .weak and .set directives, which WebAssembly's assembler drops
